evidence: Clear separation into logical modules (e.g., treebeard.mp_tree, treebeard.ns_tree, treebeard.al_tree, treebeard.ltree) with bounded responsibility for specific tree algorithms
Single Django application structure with shared core (treebeard.models.Node, treebeard.exceptions, treebeard.numconv)
No indication of inter-process communication, network boundaries, or separate deployable units — all code resides in one repository with Django-style package layout
Heavy use of Django ORM, models, and admin integration indicates tight coupling to a single runtime framework
Test suite is co-located with source and follows Django testing conventions, confirming monolithic integration
Avg fan-out of 2.48 and 5 packages suggests small-to-moderate cohesion within one cohesive system
Template tags and admin classes are integrated directly in the library rather than externalized
risks: Potential for monolithic decay if modularity boundaries are not enforced — codebases like this often blur module responsibilities over time
Testing and deployment tightly coupled — changes in one tree algorithm (e.g., MP_Tree) may impact all
Limited scalability in terms of independent evolution of features or services
